result_text:
I changed `DataExporter.java` so `all_files.zip` is built from the configured aspect names instead of fixed literals. The `reports` module tests pass offline (`mvn -q -o -pl reports test`, no output).

**What was wrong:** the zip code hard-coded `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`. When the aspect is renamed, the loose file is written as `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`, so reading the old name threw `FileNotFoundException`. The surrounding `catch (Throwable)` swallowed it, which also skipped `git-history.zip`.

**What changed**, all in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`:
- The `all_files.zip` entries are now built from the five analysis-result aspects (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other) in the same order.
- A new private helper `getScopeFileListEntry(NamedSourceCodeAspect)` takes the file name from `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call that names the loose file. It returns the `{name, content}` pair for the zip.

With the default config the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, `aspect_other.txt`. With the renamed aspect the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`.

I did not add a test for the renamed-aspect case or run the export end to end, so that path is verified by reading only.

**Not changed:** `codeanalyzer/.../landscape/analysis/LandscapeAnalyzer.java` (lines 280–284) still hard-codes the same five `aspect_*.txt` names when it reads repository file lists. A renamed aspect will likely break the landscape analysis too. I left it alone because the task is scoped to the report export.
